guides.content-brief.title: Write a brief that gives the draft direction.
guides.content-brief.description: A practical structure for describing your product, audience, evidence, and desired response.
guides.content-brief.sections.0.title: Start with one reader and one question
guides.content-brief.sections.0.body.0: Name the person this content should help and the question it should answer. “Explain how our refill works to a first-time buyer” is more useful than “make a viral video.”
guides.content-brief.sections.0.body.1: Choose one format and one main point. A short video cannot carry the same amount of detail as a buyer’s guide.
guides.content-brief.sections.1.title: Provide facts the draft can use
guides.content-brief.sections.1.body.0: List the product details that matter: what it does, what is included, where it is available, and the conditions of any offer. Include source material where possible.
guides.content-brief.sections.1.body.1: Separate verified facts from ideas to explore. Do not ask a generated narrator to describe a personal experience that never happened.
guides.content-brief.sections.2.title: Describe tone and constraints
guides.content-brief.sections.2.body.0: Give a short description of the voice and a real example if you have one. Name the claims, imagery, or terms the content must avoid.
guides.content-brief.sections.2.body.1: Provide assets you have permission to use. If product likeness matters, check the output carefully rather than assuming a generated scene will match it.
guides.content-brief.sections.3.title: Use this brief structure
guides.content-brief.sections.3.body.0: Audience: Who is this for? Question: What do they need to understand? Product facts: What can we substantiate? Direction: What format, tone, and visual references fit? Action: What should an interested person do next? Review: Who checks the finished work?
guides.content-brief.sections.4.title: Evaluate the first draft
guides.content-brief.sections.4.body.0: Read or watch the whole piece before judging individual details. Does it answer the question, use the facts correctly, and make the next step understandable?
guides.content-brief.sections.4.body.1: Fix the brief when the direction is wrong. Fix the draft when the direction is right but a detail needs work. Check the cost before generating another version.
guides.review-checklist.title: Review a draft before it represents your business.
guides.review-checklist.description: A publication checklist for generated videos, articles, and campaign creative.
guides.review-checklist.sections.0.title: Check the claim against its source
Read every statement about price, availability, results, performance, and comparisons. Verify it against a current source.
Remove invented reviews, customer experiences, and guarantees. A confident sentence is not evidence.
guides.review-checklist.sections.1.title: Inspect the full creative
For video, watch with sound and captions at phone size. Check pronunciation, continuity, product appearance, reading time, and the ending.
For an article, read the argument from beginning to end. Check citations, links, metadata, and whether the introduction promises something the article actually explains.
guides.review-checklist.sections.2.title: Check the destination and commitment
Confirm the account, URL, time, and version you intend to publish. Check where the call to action leads.
For a paid campaign, review the platform budget separately from generation credit. An approved creative does not automatically authorize every launch action.
guides.review-checklist.sections.3.title: Confirm the result
After scheduling or publishing, read the status. A submitted request can still fail because of permissions, media requirements, or a provider problem.
If a run fails, inspect completed work and charges before retrying. Keep the approved version and the actual published result distinguishable.
guides.first-channel.title: Set up your first content channel.
guides.first-channel.description: Start with a manageable publishing routine and a brief you can improve.
guides.first-channel.sections.0.title: Choose a useful starting point
guides.first-channel.sections.0.body.0: Pick one audience and one recurring subject. Name the channel so you can recognize it when reviewing jobs and scheduled posts.
guides.first-channel.sections.1.title: Set direction and budget
guides.first-channel.sections.1.body.0: Describe the product facts, tone, and intended format. Check the settings and production estimate before adding credit or starting a job.
guides.first-channel.sections.1.body.1: Set channel and account spending limits that fit your intended work. They are production controls, not promises about the number of finished pieces.
guides.first-channel.sections.2.title: Keep the first run in review
guides.first-channel.sections.2.body.0: Create one draft and inspect it completely. Check claims, creative quality, and the destination. Adjust the brief if the direction is wrong.
guides.first-channel.sections.3.title: Connect publication deliberately
guides.first-channel.sections.3.body.0: Connect the account you intend to use and confirm that the platform supports your format. Check timing and approval settings before scheduling.
guides.first-channel.sections.3.body.1: Verify the published result before expanding the routine. Recurring work still needs monitoring and review.
guides.seo-articles.title: Create an article that answers a real question.
guides.seo-articles.description: Use search research as context and your own expertise as the substance.
guides.seo-articles.sections.0.title: Choose the question before the keyword
guides.seo-articles.sections.0.body.0: Start with something your audience needs to understand. Decide what a helpful answer must contain and which product facts are relevant.
guides.seo-articles.sections.1.title: Review the structure
guides.seo-articles.sections.1.body.0: Use research to inform the outline. Remove sections that repeat the same point or do not serve the reader’s question.
guides.seo-articles.sections.1.body.1: Add examples, sources, and limitations your team can verify. Generic text becomes useful when it contains accurate, relevant detail.
guides.seo-articles.sections.2.title: Check before publishing
guides.seo-articles.sections.2.body.0: Verify claims, citations, current prices, and comparisons. Review title, description, links, and image permissions.
guides.seo-articles.sections.2.body.1: Do not describe a quality score as a ranking guarantee. Search results depend on factors beyond the generated draft.
guides.seo-articles.sections.3.title: Plan the next review
guides.seo-articles.sections.3.body.0: Revisit the page when the product or evidence changes. Track the questions it answers well and the information readers still need.
guides.agent-driven-marketing.title: Connect an agent without losing the review step.
guides.agent-driven-marketing.descriptio: Plan permissions, costs, asynchronous work, and publication decisions before automating.
guides.agent-driven-marketing.sections.0: Use the current API documentation to choose REST, Python SDK, CLI, or MCP for your environment. Confirm the endpoint and supported operations before implementing a workflow.
guides.agent-driven-marketing.sections.1: Create credentials with the access the workflow needs. Keep secrets outside source code and public briefs.
Configure budgets and review settings explicitly. A connected agent should not infer publication authority from permission to create a draft.
guides.agent-driven-marketing.sections.2: An accepted request is not a completed video or article. Poll or use supported events to read the final status and inspect output.
On failure, check completed work and charges before retrying. Do not make an unlimited retry loop around a paid operation.
guides.agent-driven-marketing.sections.3: Use a distinct approval step for publishing or spending actions. Verify account identity, destination, and the version being approved.
Check the actual result after the operation. Provider errors, missing permissions, and expired connections require a recovery path.
guides.plan-content-budget.title: Plan a content budget without guessing output counts.
guides.plan-content-budget.description: Separate the platform commitment, generation usage, and advertising spend.
guides.plan-content-budget.sections.0.ti: Define the work you want to make
guides.plan-content-budget.sections.0.bo: List the formats, lengths, and frequency you want to evaluate. Start with a modest sample rather than assuming every generated draft will be publishable.
guides.plan-content-budget.sections.1.ti: Read the estimate for your settings
guides.plan-content-budget.sections.1.bo: Video costs change with models, scenes, duration, images, voice, and music. Articles and campaign work have their own production steps.
Use the estimate shown for the actual job. A dollar credit balance is spending capacity, not a guaranteed quantity of content.
guides.plan-content-budget.sections.2.bo: Leave room for drafts you reject and work that needs another attempt. Completed paid steps can consume credit even if the entire run fails.
Someone still needs to check facts, creative quality, permissions, and the publishing result. Include that effort when comparing your options.
guides.plan-content-budget.sections.3.bo: Current prepaid packs do not renew automatically. Proposed monthly plans have a base fee and an included generation allowance, but are not yet available to purchase.
Google and Meta media spend is separate. Do not treat generation credits as an advertising budget.
